---
title: "Bet selection and staking"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-09"
abstract: |
  Papers 1 to 5 changed the model and left the betting rule alone: back the
  horse whose model win probability clears 0.15 and whose model-to-market
  ratio clears 1.3, one unit a bet. That rule is Owen's, inherited from a
  different dataset, and it has never been examined. This paper changes it
  and nothing else. The model is held fixed at paper 5's encoder — the same
  predictions paper 5 scored the test split with — while nine selection rules
  and three staking rules are searched on the 5,022 training races. One rule
  per bet type was declared by a mechanical rule and frozen before any test
  contact; the test split was then scored once.
  Nothing wins. Every declared rule loses money and every interval against
  the incumbent contains zero. The finding that matters is the control: on
  the win market, backing the market favourite flat — a rule with no model in
  it at all — returns
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); r <- targets::tar_read(p6_test_results, store = S); sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * r$roi[r$arm == "S4/K0 (market-only control)" & r$bet == "win"]) })`
  against the model rule's
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); r <- targets::tar_read(p6_test_results, store = S); sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * r$roi[r$arm == "S1/K0 (paper 5 incumbent)" & r$bet == "win"]) })`,
  its 90% interval excluding zero. The model's contribution to bet selection
  is not visible on this data. Priced at a zero-margin book the incumbent is
  roughly break-even, so the whole of its loss is the over-round — which puts
  a number on how much better a price would have to be, and that number
  cannot be checked without exchange price history the dataset does not hold.
format:

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT  <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

# Sourced robustly across the cwd tar_quarto() sets (project root) and the
# one a direct render would set (this folder).
source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_betting_strategy", "_helpers.R"))

# Every target the section files read is loaded here, centrally, so
# tar_quarto()'s dependency detection sees them: files pulled in with
# {{< include >}} are not scanned.
tar_load(c(p6_search_set_check, p6_ledger_gate, p6_rung3b_scores,
           p6_price_coverage_train, p6_overround_train,
           p6_field_sizes_train, p6_field_sizes_test,
           p6_eachway_terms_decision, p6_threshold_position_train,
           p6_incumbent_train, p6_thresholds_train, p6_contrast_check,
           p6_stage1_grid, p6_stage1_contrasts, p6_declaration,
           p6_declaration_frozen, p6_declared_rules_file,
           p6_test_arms, p6_test_results, p6_test_contrasts,
           p6_margin_decomposition, p6_fig_cumulative, p6_fig_train_vs_test,
           p6_test_report_file, p6_declared_selection_sizes, p6_universe,
           p6_kelly_edge_share),
         store = P6_STORE)

n_train_races <- p6_universe$n_train_races
n_test_races  <- p6_universe$n_test_races
```
